items.text: The U.S. military disabled a cargo ship that tried to run its blockade of Iranian ports, striking the Pacific Archer's stern from the air, Central Command said Friday.
items.detail: CENTCOM said a U.S. military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the Palau-flagged bulk carrier M/V Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday after the ship left Iran's Bandar Abbas port and ignored multiple warnings; its propulsion was disabled and the civilian crew was unharmed. Ship-tracking sites listed its destination as Singapore, AP reported. CENTCOM said U.S. forces have redirected 158 compliant commercial ships and disabled six that refused during the blockade, which resumed in mid-July. Iran's navy chief, Rear Adm. Shahram Irani, said on state TV that Iran will carry out operations to break the blockade, and Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, said the Strait of Hormuz will not be reopened. The war reaches nine months on Saturday.
items.why: Each forced stop raises the risk of a direct clash at sea as Iran vows to break the blockade, keeping Gulf shipping and oil prices on edge.

items.text: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% in Friday's shortened post-Thanksgiving session, finishing its best week since April 2025 with a 5.6% gain.
items.detail: The S&P 500 closed at 7,297.49, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 591.99 points (1.2%) to 50,774.94, and the Nasdaq composite rose 2.3% to 24,129.50. For the week the S&P 500 gained 5.6%, the Dow 5.5% and the Nasdaq 6.7%, a sharp turnaround from the prior week, when the S&P 500 finished more than 10% below last month's record high. Technology stocks led again, but about 4 of every 5 stocks in the index rose. Markets closed early at 1 p.m. ET after being shut Thursday for Thanksgiving.
items.why: The rebound erases much of the recent correction that hit retirement and investment accounts.

items.text: Quebec's Bill 21, which bars many public workers from wearing religious symbols on the job, was largely upheld Friday by the Supreme Court of Canada.
items.detail: In English Montreal School Board v. Quebec (2026 SCC 41), the court ruled Quebec validly used the Charter's notwithstanding clause to shield the 2019 secularism law, reaffirming its 1988 Ford ruling that the override has no limits beyond its text; six of the seven judges joined that holding. The one part struck down: the face-covering rule cannot apply to elected members of Quebec's National Assembly, which violates the Charter right to seek office and sit as a legislator. The court said judges may still declare a law inconsistent with the Charter despite the override, but four of the seven declined to do so here; Justices Karakatsanis, Kasirer and O'Bonsawin wrote that the law infringes religious freedom, expression and equality. Challenges brought by Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers and the English Montreal School Board were dismissed. Prime Minister Mark Carney said his government would study the ruling.
items.why: The ruling confirms provinces can override Charter rights with few limits, keeping hijab-, turban- and cross-wearing teachers and officials out of many Quebec public jobs.

items.text: The Thanksgiving storm's power outages fell by half Friday from a peak above 900,000 as rain eased, and Macy's postponed parade is set for Saturday.
items.detail: PowerOutage.us data showed outages, which peaked Thursday above 900,000 homes and businesses, were down about 50% by Friday afternoon, AP reported. Coastal flood warnings stayed up from New Jersey to Virginia. Roofs collapsed in Ocean City and Rockville; Norfolk, Va., crews rescued 39 people; and part of a fishing pier collapsed in Virginia Beach, closing about 3 miles of beach and the boardwalk. Wet snow fell as far south as the Tennessee Valley and freezing rain hit northern New England. New York City prepared to hold Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade on Saturday after its unprecedented rain-and-wind postponement.
items.why: Hundreds of thousands were still without power as holiday travelers headed home.

items.text: Ukraine's attack in Libya's port of Benghazi violated Libyan sovereignty and risks spreading the war to the Mediterranean, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni told Zelenskyy Friday.
items.detail: In a phone call, Meloni reaffirmed Italy's support for Ukraine toward a just and lasting peace but said it cannot extend to accepting operations that put Italy's and the region's security at risk, her office said. Zelenskyy confirmed the operation was carried out without prior coordination with partners and pledged full information sharing and direct, constant contact. The operation in Benghazi, which Ukraine said sank the Russian corvette Merkury, was reported Nov. 23.
items.why: A key European backer publicly rebuked Kyiv for taking the fight to the Mediterranean.

items.text: A DEA tip line seeking anonymous reports on cartel members and corrupt officials in Sinaloa drew a formal complaint from Mexico, President Claudia Sheinbaum said Friday.
items.detail: Sheinbaum told her daily briefing the relationship with the U.S. is "one of coordination, not subordination" and called the tip line interference in Mexico's internal affairs. DEA chief Terry Cole announced the line on Wednesday for information on members of designated terrorist organizations, the officials who support them and money launderers in Sinaloa, and said one for Jalisco is planned. The dispute comes days after Mexico, with help from a U.S. surveillance drone, captured Sinaloa trafficker Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, "El Chapo Isidro"; Mexico's attorney general said he will be tried in Mexico despite a U.S. extradition request.
items.why: The spat strains cooperation with the main partner in U.S. efforts against fentanyl trafficking.

items.text: Norse Atlantic Airways, a low-fare transatlantic carrier, filed for bankruptcy Friday and canceled all flights, blaming fuel costs driven up by the Iran war.
items.detail: The Norwegian operating unit of the long-haul carrier filed for bankruptcy after failing to secure short-term funding, a day after it suspended flights; lessors had served termination notices on all 12 of its Boeing 787s. The UK subsidiary's flights were also canceled and ticket sales halted while the group seeks a way to keep that unit running. Norse, founded in 2021, flew between the U.S. and Europe and to Asia and South Africa; it told passengers not to go to airports and to contact travel agents, insurers or card issuers. Jet fuel prices have roughly doubled since the Iran war began in February.
items.why: Travelers holding Norse tickets, including many in the U.S., are stranded or out of a flight.

items.text: South Africa's National Health Insurance Act survived its main court test Friday, as the Constitutional Court dismissed challenges to how Parliament passed it.
items.detail: The Constitutional Court dismissed applications by the Board of Healthcare Funders and the Western Cape provincial government, finding Parliament's public participation process on the 2023 NHI Act met constitutional requirements, the Department of Health said. The law aims to create a single state-run fund to pay for universal health coverage. The department said it will announce the next steps for putting the NHI into effect later.
items.why: The ruling clears a key hurdle for one of the world's largest overhauls of a national health system.
